description: Our team is building an interactive Martian survival map: a guide that shows future explorers where to land, where to find water ice, which terrain is safe to cross, and where radiation, dust storms, and extreme cold pose the greatest risks. By combining real NASA Mars data into one easy-to-use map, we turn a hostile planet into a place humans can plan to live on.
summary:
Martian Map is an interactive tool for exploring Mars and planning a possible mission route. Users can choose a starting point and destination, compare routes, and explore terrain, mission sites, seasons, resources, and estimated hazards.

It addresses the challenge by bringing route planning and Mars data into one accessible map. NASA MOLA topography and Mars Trek imagery provide regional context, while the app explains where it uses estimates for factors such as ice, solar power, and communications.

The project matters because planning for Mars means weighing many trade-offs across a harsh, unfamiliar landscape. Martian Map helps people see those choices, understand the evidence behind them, and recognize the uncertainty in the data. It is an educational tool, not a guide for real mission decisions.
details:
Martian Map helps people explore what a journey across Mars might involve. You can spin the planet, choose a starting point and destination, and compare possible routes by distance, terrain, travel time, and estimated risks. You can also explore mission sites, Mars seasons, and the NASA data behind the map.

We built it to make Mars exploration easier to understand. The map uses NASA’s MOLA data for broad elevation and terrain patterns, along with imagery from NASA Mars Trek. Some values—such as water ice, solar power, temperature, and communication—are estimates from our model, so the scores are for learning and comparison, not real mission decisions. The terrain data is regional and cannot show every hazard a crew might encounter.

The project was made with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Three.js. We wanted users to see not just a route, but the choices and uncertainties behind it. OpenAI Codex and Claude assisted with development.
